subject: POC capacity planning - next steps and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC capacity planning - next steps and success criteria

Thanks again for the call earlier, Alex - good alignment overall. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scheduled for mid-June. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

Summary of success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: median request latency <= 150ms for 95% of requests on the evaluation dataset.
- Throughput: support sustained 120 requests/minute with 2k average tokens per request during peak tests.
- Quality: top-1 response match rate >= 92% against your reference prompts for the retrieval-augmented generator.
- Stability: no more than 1x incident requiring manual intervention during the 2-week evaluation window.

Evaluation plan / ownership:
- Acme: provide sample traffic patterns (payload size, concurrency) and a 3-day golden prompt set for automated scoring (Owner: Alex).
- Redwood: provision POC environment, reserved GPUs, autoscaling policy, and eval harness (Owner: Marissa / Ethan).
- Schedules: kickoff 2026-06-15, evaluation window 2026-06-16 -> 2026-06-30.

Capacity asks for initial planning (need your confirmation on expected peak):
- Model: 16B decoder (we recommend the quantized variant unless you need fp16).
- Expected sustained concurrency during peak testing: 10 concurrent sessions (you indicated ~8-12).
- Burst expectations: ability to handle short bursts up to 4x sustained for 2-5 minutes.

Next steps:
1) Alex: confirm the dataset and expected concurrency/burst numbers (reply).
2) Ethan: can you review and propose reserved GPU sizing + autoscale config?
3) I will send a kickoff invite for 2026-06-15 once capacity is confirmed.

Attachments: poc_success_criteria.md, redwood_poc_template.pdf (POC template + eval checklist)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks for the context. Proposal below - we can have this provisioned and ready for the 2026-06-15 kickoff.

Provisioning plan (recommended):
- Reserved hardware: 2x A100 80GB (dedicated) assigned to Acme POC cluster. These map to our Dedicated offering and avoid noisy neighbor variability.
- Autoscaling: use a warm-pool based autoscaler with the following settings: min_instances = 1, target_instances = 2 (sustained), max_instances = 4 (burst). Burst scale-up target latency-aware: scale to max within 60s for CPU/GPU headroom triggers.
- Warm pool: keep 1 pre-warmed instance (model loaded) to limit cold-starts. Pre-warm policy will hold the model in memory for up to 15 minutes of idle time.
- Model config: deploy 16B quantized variant (int8) to reduce memory needs and improve throughput; we can switch to fp16 if you want to test exact quality differences.
- Observability: enable token-level latency and cost traces; provide per-route dashboards for the eval prompts.

Estimated cost (30-day projection, heavily dependent on hours):
- Baseline (2x dedicated A100): ~$6,400/mo (pro rata for POC window).
- If bursting to 4x for load tests, incremental hourly costs apply (~+100% while bursted). I'll include a short ops note file with a week-by-week callout.

Attachments: capacity_plan_ops_notes.txt

If that's acceptable I'll schedule the provisioning for 2026-06-14 (so the environment is ready on 06-15). Also recommend we enable a short warm-up test on 06-15 morning to validate latency targets before handing over to Acme.

- Ethan Park
